你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

- 运行一个示例。

- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。

1. 实践目标。

3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案
```

```md
## 5. 综合实践
```

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

schema.name: Agent
schema.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

16	def to_tensor(
17	    data: Union[torch.Tensor, np.ndarray, Sequence, int,
18	                float]) -> torch.Tensor:
19	    """Convert objects of various python types to :obj:`torch.Tensor`.
20	
21	    Supported types are: :class:`numpy.ndarray`, :class:`torch.Tensor`,
22	    :class:`Sequence`, :class:`int` and :class:`float`.
23	
24	    Args:
25	        data (torch.Tensor | numpy.ndarray | Sequence | int | float): Data to
26	            be converted.
27	
28	    Returns:
29	        torch.Tensor: the converted data.
30	    """
31	
32	    if isinstance(data, torch.Tensor):
33	        return data
34	    elif isinstance(data, np.ndarray):
35	        if data.dtype is dtype('float64'):
36	            data = data.astype(np.float32)
37	        return torch.from_numpy(data)
38	    elif isinstance(data, Sequence) and not mmengine.is_str(data):
39	        return torch.tensor(data)
40	    elif isinstance(data, int):
41	        return torch.LongTensor([data])
42	    elif isinstance(data, float):
43	        return torch.FloatTensor([data])
44	    else:
45	        raise TypeError(f'type {type(data)} cannot be converted to tensor.')

48	@TRANSFORMS.register_module()
49	class Pack3DDetInputs(BaseTransform):
50	    INPUTS_KEYS = ['points', 'img']
51	    INSTANCEDATA_3D_KEYS = [
52	        'gt_bboxes_3d', 'gt_labels_3d', 'attr_labels', 'depths', 'centers_2d'
53	    ]
54	    INSTANCEDATA_2D_KEYS = [
55	        'gt_bboxes',
56	        'gt_bboxes_labels',
57	    ]
58	
59	    SEG_KEYS = [
60	        'gt_seg_map', 'pts_instance_mask', 'pts_semantic_mask',
61	        'gt_semantic_seg'
62	    ]
63	
64	    def __init__(
65	        self,
66	        keys: tuple,
67	        meta_keys: tuple = ('img_path', 'ori_shape', 'img_shape', 'lidar2img',
68	                            'depth2img', 'cam2img', 'pad_shape',
69	                            'scale_factor', 'flip', 'pcd_horizontal_flip',
70	                            'pcd_vertical_flip', 'box_mode_3d', 'box_type_3d',
71	                            'img_norm_cfg', 'num_pts_feats', 'pcd_trans',
72	                            'sample_idx', 'pcd_scale_factor', 'pcd_rotation',
73	                            'pcd_rotation_angle', 'lidar_path',
74	                            'transformation_3d_flow', 'trans_mat',
75	                            'affine_aug', 'sweep_img_metas', 'ori_cam2img',
76	                            'cam2global', 'crop_offset', 'img_crop_offset',
77	                            'resize_img_shape', 'lidar2cam', 'ori_lidar2img',
78	                            'num_ref_frames', 'num_views', 'ego2global',
79	                            'axis_align_matrix')
80	    ) -> None:
81	        self.keys = keys
82	        self.meta_keys = meta_keys
83	
84	    def _remove_prefix(self, key: str) -> str:
85	        if key.startswith('gt_'):
86	            key = key[3:]
87	        return key
88	
89	    def transform(self, results: Union[dict,
90	                                       List[dict]]) -> Union[dict, List[dict]]:
91	        """Method to pack the input data. when the value in this dict is a
92	        list, it usually is in Augmentations Testing.
93	
94	        Args:
95	            results (dict | list[dict]): Result dict from the data pipeline.
96	
97	        Returns:
98	            dict | List[dict]:
99	
100	            - 'inputs' (dict): The forward data of models. It usually contains
101	              following keys:
102	
103	                - points
104	                - img
105	
106	            - 'data_samples' (:obj:`Det3DDataSample`): The annotation info of
107	              the sample.
108	        """
109	        # augtest
110	        if isinstance(results, list):
111	            if len(results) == 1:
112	                # simple test
113	                return self.pack_single_results(results[0])
114	            pack_results = []
115	            for single_result in results:
116	                pack_results.append(self.pack_single_results(single_result))
117	            return pack_results
118	        # norm training and simple testing
119	        elif isinstance(results, dict):
120	            return self.pack_single_results(results)
121	        else:
122	            raise NotImplementedError
123	
124	    def pack_single_results(self, results: dict) -> dict:
125	        """Method to pack the single input data. when the value in this dict is
126	        a list, it usually is in Augmentations Testing.
127	
128	        Args:
129	            results (dict): Result dict from the data pipeline.
130	
131	        Returns:
132	            dict: A dict contains
133	
134	            - 'inputs' (dict): The forward data of models. It usually contains
135	              following keys:
136	
137	                - points
138	                - img
139	
140	            - 'data_samples' (:obj:`Det3DDataSample`): The annotation info
141	              of the sample.
142	        """
143	        # Format 3D data
144	        if 'points' in results:
145	            if isinstance(results['points'], BasePoints):
146	                results['points'] = results['points'].tensor
147	
148	        if 'img' in results:
149	            if isinstance(results['img'], list):
150	                # process multiple imgs in single frame
151	                imgs = np.stack(results['img'], axis=0)
152	                if imgs.flags.c_contiguous:
153	                    imgs = to_tensor(imgs).permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
154	                else:
155	                    imgs = to_tensor(
156	                        np.ascontiguousarray(imgs.transpose(0, 3, 1, 2)))
157	                results['img'] = imgs
158	            else:
159	                img = results['img']
160	                if len(img.shape) < 3:
161	                    img = np.expand_dims(img, -1)
162	                # To improve the computational speed by by 3-5 times, apply:
163	                # `torch.permute()` rather than `np.transpose()`.
164	                # Refer to https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection/pull/9533
165	                # for more details
166	                if img.flags.c_contiguous:
167	                    img = to_tensor(img).permute(2, 0, 1).contiguous()
168	                else:
169	                    img = to_tensor(
170	                        np.ascontiguousarray(img.transpose(2, 0, 1)))
171	                results['img'] = img
172	
173	        for key in [
174	                'proposals', 'gt_bboxes', 'gt_bboxes_ignore', 'gt_labels',
175	                'gt_bboxes_labels', 'attr_labels', 'pts_instance_mask',
176	                'pts_semantic_mask', 'centers_2d', 'depths', 'gt_labels_3d'
177	        ]:
178	            if key not in results:
179	                continue
180	            if isinstance(results[key], list):
181	                results[key] = [to_tensor(res) for res in results[key]]
182	            else:
183	                results[key] = to_tensor(results[key])
184	        if 'gt_bboxes_3d' in results:
185	            if not isinstance(results['gt_bboxes_3d'], BaseInstance3DBoxes):
186	                results['gt_bboxes_3d'] = to_tensor(results['gt_bboxes_3d'])
187	
188	        if 'gt_semantic_seg' in results:
189	            results['gt_semantic_seg'] = to_tensor(
190	                results['gt_semantic_seg'][None])
191	        if 'gt_seg_map' in results:
192	            results['gt_seg_map'] = results['gt_seg_map'][None, ...]
193	
194	        data_sample = Det3DDataSample()
195	        gt_instances_3d = InstanceData()
196	        gt_instances = InstanceData()
197	        gt_pts_seg = PointData()
198	
199	        data_metas = {}
200	        for key in self.meta_keys:
201	            if key in results:
202	                data_metas[key] = results[key]
203	            elif 'images' in results:
204	                if len(results['images'].keys()) == 1:
205	                    cam_type = list(results['images'].keys())[0]
206	                    # single-view image
207	                    if key in results['images'][cam_type]:
208	                        data_metas[key] = results['images'][cam_type][key]
209	                else:
210	                    # multi-view image
211	                    img_metas = []
212	                    cam_types = list(results['images'].keys())
213	                    for cam_type in cam_types:
214	                        if key in results['images'][cam_type]:
215	                            img_metas.append(results['images'][cam_type][key])
216	                    if len(img_metas) > 0:
217	                        data_metas[key] = img_metas
218	            elif 'lidar_points' in results:
219	                if key in results['lidar_points']:
220	                    data_metas[key] = results['lidar_points'][key]
221	        data_sample.set_metainfo(data_metas)
222	
223	        inputs = {}
224	        for key in self.keys:
225	            if key in results:
226	                if key in self.INPUTS_KEYS:
227	                    inputs[key] = results[key]
228	                elif key in self.INSTANCEDATA_3D_KEYS:
229	                    gt_instances_3d[self._remove_prefix(key)] = results[key]
230	                elif key in self.INSTANCEDATA_2D_KEYS:
231	                    if key == 'gt_bboxes_labels':
232	                        gt_instances['labels'] = results[key]
233	                    else:
234	                        gt_instances[self._remove_prefix(key)] = results[key]
235	                elif key in self.SEG_KEYS:
236	                    gt_pts_seg[self._remove_prefix(key)] = results[key]
237	                else:
238	                    raise NotImplementedError(f'Please modified '
239	                                              f'`Pack3DDetInputs` '
240	                                              f'to put {key} to '
241	                                              f'corresponding field')
242	
243	        data_sample.gt_instances_3d = gt_instances_3d
244	        data_sample.gt_instances = gt_instances
245	        data_sample.gt_pts_seg = gt_pts_seg
246	        if 'eval_ann_info' in results:
247	            data_sample.eval_ann_info = results['eval_ann_info']
248	        else:
249	            data_sample.eval_ann_info = None
250	
251	        packed_results = dict()
252	        packed_results['data_samples'] = data_sample
253	        packed_results['inputs'] = inputs
254	
255	        return packed_results
256	
257	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
258	        """str: Return a string that describes the module."""
259	        repr_str = self.__class__.__name__
260	        repr_str += f'(keys={self.keys})'
261	        repr_str += f'(meta_keys={self.meta_keys})'
262	        return repr_str

11	class Det3DDataSample(DetDataSample):
12	    """A data structure interface of MMDetection3D. They are used as interfaces
13	    between different components.
14	
15	    The attributes in ``Det3DDataSample`` are divided into several parts:
16	
17	        - ``proposals`` (InstanceData): Region proposals used in two-stage
18	          detectors.
19	        - ``ignored_instances`` (InstanceData): Instances to be ignored during
20	          training/testing.
21	        - ``gt_instances_3d`` (InstanceData): Ground truth of 3D instance
22	          annotations.
23	        - ``gt_instances`` (InstanceData): Ground truth of 2D instance
24	          annotations.
25	        - ``pred_instances_3d`` (InstanceData): 3D instances of model
26	          predictions.
27	          - For point-cloud 3D object detection task whose input modality is
28	            `use_lidar=True, use_camera=False`, the 3D predictions results are
29	            saved in `pred_instances_3d`.
30	          - For vision-only (monocular/multi-view) 3D object detection task
31	            whose input modality is `use_lidar=False, use_camera=True`, the 3D
32	            predictions are saved in `pred_instances_3d`.
33	        - ``pred_instances`` (InstanceData): 2D instances of model predictions.
34	          - For multi-modality 3D detection task whose input modality is
35	            `use_lidar=True, use_camera=True`, the 2D predictions are saved in
36	            `pred_instances`.
37	        - ``pts_pred_instances_3d`` (InstanceData): 3D instances of model
38	          predictions based on point cloud.
39	          - For multi-modality 3D detection task whose input modality is
40	            `use_lidar=True, use_camera=True`, the 3D predictions based on
41	            point cloud are saved in `pts_pred_instances_3d` to distinguish
42	            with `img_pred_instances_3d` which based on image.
43	        - ``img_pred_instances_3d`` (InstanceData): 3D instances of model
44	          predictions based on image.
45	          - For multi-modality 3D detection task whose input modality is
46	            `use_lidar=True, use_camera=True`, the 3D predictions based on
47	            image are saved in `img_pred_instances_3d` to distinguish with
48	            `pts_pred_instances_3d` which based on point cloud.
49	        - ``gt_pts_seg`` (PointData): Ground truth of point cloud segmentation.
50	        - ``pred_pts_seg`` (PointData): Prediction of point cloud segmentation.
51	        - ``eval_ann_info`` (dict or None): Raw annotation, which will be
52	          passed to evaluator and do the online evaluation.
53	
54	    Examples:
55	        >>> import torch
56	        >>> from mmengine.structures import InstanceData
57	
58	        >>> from mmdet3d.structures import Det3DDataSample
59	        >>> from mmdet3d.structures.bbox_3d import BaseInstance3DBoxes
60	
61	        >>> data_sample = Det3DDataSample()
62	        >>> meta_info = dict(
63	        ...     img_shape=(800, 1196, 3),

# dataset settings
dataset_type = 'KittiDataset'
data_root = 'data/kitti/'
class_names = ['Pedestrian', 'Cyclist', 'Car']
point_cloud_range = [0, -40, -3, 70.4, 40, 1]
input_modality = dict(use_lidar=True, use_camera=False)
metainfo = dict(classes=class_names)

# Example to use different file client
# Method 1: simply set the data root and let the file I/O module
# automatically infer from prefix (not support LMDB and Memcache yet)

# data_root = 's3://openmmlab/datasets/detection3d/kitti/'

# Method 2: Use backend_args, file_client_args in versions before 1.1.0
# backend_args = dict(
#     backend='petrel',
#     path_mapping=dict({
#         './data/': 's3://openmmlab/datasets/detection3d/',
#          'data/': 's3://openmmlab/datasets/detection3d/'
#      }))
backend_args = None

db_sampler = dict(
    data_root=data_root,
    info_path=data_root + 'kitti_dbinfos_train.pkl',
    rate=1.0,
    prepare=dict(
        filter_by_difficulty=[-1],
        filter_by_min_points=dict(Car=5, Pedestrian=10, Cyclist=10)),
    classes=class_names,
    sample_groups=dict(Car=12, Pedestrian=6, Cyclist=6),
    points_loader=dict(
        type='LoadPointsFromFile',
        coord_type='LIDAR',
        load_dim=4,
        use_dim=4,
        backend_args=backend_args),
    backend_args=backend_args)

train_pipeline = [
    dict(
        type='LoadPointsFromFile',
        coord_type='LIDAR',
        load_dim=4,  # x, y, z, intensity
        use_dim=4,
        backend_args=backend_args),
    dict(type='LoadAnnotations3D', with_bbox_3d=True, with_label_3d=True),
    dict(type='ObjectSample', db_sampler=db_sampler),
    dict(
        type='ObjectNoise',
        num_try=100,
        translation_std=[1.0, 1.0, 0.5],
        global_rot_range=[0.0, 0.0],
        rot_range=[-0.78539816, 0.78539816]),
    dict(type='RandomFlip3D', flip_ratio_bev_horizontal=0.5),
    dict(
        type='GlobalRotScaleTrans',
        rot_range=[-0.78539816, 0.78539816],
        scale_ratio_range=[0.95, 1.05]),
    dict(type='PointsRangeFilter', point_cloud_range=point_cloud_range),
    dict(type='ObjectRangeFilter', point_cloud_range=point_cloud_range),
    dict(type='PointShuffle'),
    dict(
        type='Pack3DDetInputs',
        keys=['points', 'gt_bboxes_3d', 'gt_labels_3d'])
]
test_pipeline = [
    dict(
        type='LoadPointsFromFile',
        coord_type='LIDAR',
        load_dim=4,
        use_dim=4,
        backend_args=backend_args),
    dict(
        type='MultiScaleFlipAug3D',
        img_scale=(1333, 800),
        pts_scale_ratio=1,
        flip=False,
        transforms=[
            dict(
                type='GlobalRotScaleTrans',
                rot_range=[0, 0],
                scale_ratio_range=[1., 1.],
                translation_std=[0, 0, 0]),
            dict(type='RandomFlip3D'),
            dict(
                type='PointsRangeFilter', point_cloud_range=point_cloud_range)
        ]),
    dict(type='Pack3DDetInputs', keys=['points'])
]
# construct a pipeline for data and gt loading in show function
# please keep its loading function consistent with test_pipeline (e.g. client)
eval_pipeline = [
    dict(
        type='LoadPointsFromFile',
        coord_type='LIDAR',
        load_dim=4,
        use_dim=4,
        backend_args=backend_args),
    dict(type='Pack3DDetInputs', keys=['points'])
]
train_dataloader = dict(
    batch_size=6,
    num_workers=4,
    persistent_workers=True,
    sampler=dict(type='DefaultSampler', shuffle=True),
    dataset=dict(
        type='RepeatDataset',
        times=2,
        dataset=dict(
            type=dataset_type,
            data_root=data_root,
            ann_file='kitti_infos_train.pkl',
            data_prefix=dict(pts='training/velodyne_reduced'),
            pipeline=train_pipeline,
            modality=input_modality,
            test_mode=False,
            metainfo=metainfo,
            # we use box_type_3d='LiDAR' in kitti and nuscenes dataset
            # and box_type_3d='Depth' in sunrgbd and scannet dataset.
            box_type_3d='LiDAR',
            backend_args=backend_args)))
val_dataloader = dict(
    batch_size=1,
    num_workers=1,
    persistent_workers=True,
    drop_last=False,
    sampler=dict(type='DefaultSampler', shuffle=False),
    dataset=dict(
        type=dataset_type,
        data_root=data_root,
        data_prefix=dict(pts='training/velodyne_reduced'),
        ann_file='kitti_infos_val.pkl',
        pipeline=test_pipeline,
        modality=input_modality,
        test_mode=True,
        metainfo=metainfo,
        box_type_3d='LiDAR',
        backend_args=backend_args))
test_dataloader = dict(
    batch_size=1,
    num_workers=1,
    persistent_workers=True,
    drop_last=False,
    sampler=dict(type='DefaultSampler', shuffle=False),
    dataset=dict(
        type=dataset_type,
        data_root=data_root,
        data_prefix=dict(pts='training/velodyne_reduced'),
        ann_file='kitti_infos_val.pkl',
        pipeline=test_pipeline,
        modality=input_modality,
        test_mode=True,
        metainfo=metainfo,
        box_type_3d='LiDAR',
        backend_args=backend_args))
val_evaluator = dict(
    type='KittiMetric',
    ann_file=data_root + 'kitti_infos_val.pkl',
    metric='bbox',
    backend_args=backend_args)
test_evaluator = val_evaluator

vis_backends = [dict(type='LocalVisBackend')]
visualizer = dict(
    type='Det3DLocalVisualizer', vis_backends=vis_backends, name='visualizer')

12	from torch import Tensor

15	from mmdet3d.registry import MODELS
16	from mmdet3d.structures.det3d_data_sample import SampleList
17	from mmdet3d.utils import OptConfigType
18	from .utils import multiview_img_stack_batch
19	from .voxelize import VoxelizationByGridShape, dynamic_scatter_3d

22	@MODELS.register_module()
23	class Det3DDataPreprocessor(DetDataPreprocessor):
24	    """Points / Image pre-processor for point clouds / vision-only / multi-
25	    modality 3D detection tasks.
26	
27	    It provides the data pre-processing as follows
28	
29	    - Collate and move image and point cloud data to the target device.
30	
31	    - 1) For image data:
32	
33	      - Pad images in inputs to the maximum size of current batch with defined
34	        ``pad_value``. The padding size can be divisible by a defined
35	        ``pad_size_divisor``.
36	      - Stack images in inputs to batch_imgs.
37	      - Convert images in inputs from bgr to rgb if the shape of input is
38	        (3, H, W).
39	      - Normalize images in inputs with defined std and mean.
40	      - Do batch augmentations during training.
41	
42	    - 2) For point cloud data:
43	
44	      - If no voxelization, directly return list of point cloud data.
45	      - If voxelization is applied, voxelize point cloud according to
46	        ``voxel_type`` and obtain ``voxels``.
47	
48	    Args:
49	        voxel (bool): Whether to apply voxelization to point cloud.
50	            Defaults to False.
51	        voxel_type (str): Voxelization type. Two voxelization types are
52	            provided: 'hard' and 'dynamic', respectively for hard voxelization
53	            and dynamic voxelization. Defaults to 'hard'.
54	        voxel_layer (dict or :obj:`ConfigDict`, optional): Voxelization layer
55	            config. Defaults to None.
56	        batch_first (bool): Whether to put the batch dimension to the first
57	            dimension when getting voxel coordinates. Defaults to True.
58	        max_voxels (int, optional): Maximum number of voxels in each voxel
59	            grid. Defaults to None.
60	        mean (Sequence[Number], optional): The pixel mean of R, G, B channels.
61	            Defaults to None.
62	        std (Sequence[Number], optional): The pixel standard deviation of
63	            R, G, B channels. Defaults to None.
64	        pad_size_divisor (int): The size of padded image should be divisible by
65	            ``pad_size_divisor``. Defaults to 1.
66	        pad_value (float or int): The padded pixel value. Defaults to 0.
67	        pad_mask (bool): Whether to pad instance masks. Defaults to False.
68	        mask_pad_value (int): The padded pixel value for instance masks.
69	            Defaults to 0.
70	        pad_seg (bool): Whether to pad semantic segmentation maps.
71	            Defaults to False.
72	        seg_pad_value (int): The padded pixel value for semantic segmentation
73	            maps. Defaults to 255.
74	        bgr_to_rgb (bool): Whether to convert image from BGR to RGB.
75	            Defaults to False.
76	        rgb_to_bgr (bool): Whether to convert image from RGB to BGR.
77	            Defaults to False.
78	        boxtype2tensor (bool): Whether to convert the ``BaseBoxes`` type of
79	            bboxes data to ``Tensor`` type. Defaults to True.
80	        non_blocking (bool): Whether to block current process when transferring
81	            data to device. Defaults to False.
82	        batch_augments (List[dict], optional): Batch-level augmentations.
83	            Defaults to None.
84	    """
85	
86	    def __init__(self,
87	                 voxel: bool = False,
88	                 voxel_type: str = 'hard',
89	                 voxel_layer: OptConfigType = None,
90	                 batch_first: bool = True,
91	                 max_voxels: Optional[int] = None,
92	                 mean: Sequence[Number] = None,
93	                 std: Sequence[Number] = None,
94	                 pad_size_divisor: int = 1,
95	                 pad_value: Union[float, int] = 0,
96	                 pad_mask: bool = False,
97	                 mask_pad_value: int = 0,
98	                 pad_seg: bool = False,
99	                 seg_pad_value: int = 255,
100	                 bgr_to_rgb: bool = False,
101	                 rgb_to_bgr: bool = False,
102	                 boxtype2tensor: bool = True,
103	                 non_blocking: bool = False,
104	                 batch_augments: Optional[List[dict]] = None) -> None:
105	        super(Det3DDataPreprocessor, self).__init__(
106	            mean=mean,
107	            std=std,
108	            pad_size_divisor=pad_size_divisor,
109	            pad_value=pad_value,
110	            pad_mask=pad_mask,
111	            mask_pad_value=mask_pad_value,
112	            pad_seg=pad_seg,
113	            seg_pad_value=seg_pad_value,
114	            bgr_to_rgb=bgr_to_rgb,
115	            rgb_to_bgr=rgb_to_bgr,
116	            boxtype2tensor=boxtype2tensor,
117	            non_blocking=non_blocking,
118	            batch_augments=batch_augments)
119	        self.voxel = voxel
120	        self.voxel_type = voxel_type
121	        self.batch_first = batch_first
122	        self.max_voxels = max_voxels
123	        if voxel:
124	            self.voxel_layer = VoxelizationByGridShape(**voxel_layer)
125	
126	    def forward(self,
127	                data: Union[dict, List[dict]],
128	                training: bool = False) -> Union[dict, List[dict]]:
129	        """Perform normalization, padding and bgr2rgb conversion based on
130	        ``BaseDataPreprocessor``.
131	
132	        Args:
133	            data (dict or List[dict]): Data from dataloader. The dict contains
134	                the whole batch data, when it is a list[dict], the list
135	                indicates test time augmentation.
136	            training (bool): Whether to enable training time augmentation.
137	                Defaults to False.
138	
139	        Returns:
140	            dict or List[dict]: Data in the same format as the model input.
141	        """
142	        if isinstance(data, list):
143	            num_augs = len(data)
144	            aug_batch_data = []
145	            for aug_id in range(num_augs):
146	                single_aug_batch_data = self.simple_process(
147	                    data[aug_id], training)
148	                aug_batch_data.append(single_aug_batch_data)
149	            return aug_batch_data
150	
151	        else:
152	            return self.simple_process(data, training)
153	
154	    def simple_process(self, data: dict, training: bool = False) -> dict:
155	        """Perform normalization, padding and bgr2rgb conversion for img data
156	        based on ``BaseDataPreprocessor``, and voxelize point cloud if `voxel`
157	        is set to be True.
158	
159	        Args:
160	            data (dict): Data sampled from dataloader.
161	            training (bool): Whether to enable training time augmentation.
162	                Defaults to False.
163	
164	        Returns:
165	            dict: Data in the same format as the model input.
166	        """
167	        if 'img' in data['inputs']:
168	            batch_pad_shape = self._get_pad_shape(data)
169	
170	        data = self.collate_data(data)
171	        inputs, data_samples = data['inputs'], data['data_samples']
172	        batch_inputs = dict()
173	
174	        if 'points' in inputs:
175	            batch_inputs['points'] = inputs['points']
176	
177	            if self.voxel:
178	                voxel_dict = self.voxelize(inputs['points'], data_samples)
179	                batch_inputs['voxels'] = voxel_dict
180	
181	        if 'imgs' in inputs:
182	            imgs = inputs['imgs']
183	
184	            if data_samples is not None:
185	                # NOTE the batched image size information may be useful, e.g.
186	                # in DETR, this is needed for the construction of masks, which
187	                # is then used for the transformer_head.
188	                batch_input_shape = tuple(imgs[0].size()[-2:])
189	                for data_sample, pad_shape in zip(data_samples,
190	                                                  batch_pad_shape):
191	                    data_sample.set_metainfo({
192	                        'batch_input_shape': batch_input_shape,
193	                        'pad_shape': pad_shape
194	                    })
195	
196	                if self.boxtype2tensor:
197	                    samplelist_boxtype2tensor(data_samples)
198	                if self.pad_mask:
199	                    self.pad_gt_masks(data_samples)
200	                if self.pad_seg:
201	                    self.pad_gt_sem_seg(data_samples)
202	
203	            if training and self.batch_augments is not None:
204	                for batch_aug in self.batch_augments:
205	                    imgs, data_samples = batch_aug(imgs, data_samples)
206	            batch_inputs['imgs'] = imgs
207	
208	        return {'inputs': batch_inputs, 'data_samples': data_samples}
209	
210	    def preprocess_img(self, _batch_img: Tensor) -> Tensor:
211	        # channel transform
212	        if self._channel_conversion:
213	            _batch_img = _batch_img[[2, 1, 0], ...]
214	        # Convert to float after channel conversion to ensure
215	        # efficiency
216	        _batch_img = _batch_img.float()
217	        # Normalization.
218	        if self._enable_normalize:
219	            if self.mean.shape[0] == 3:
220	                assert _batch_img.dim() == 3 and _batch_img.shape[0] == 3, (
221	                    'If the mean has 3 values, the input tensor '
222	                    'should in shape of (3, H, W), but got the '
223	                    f'tensor with shape {_batch_img.shape}')
224	            _batch_img = (_batch_img - self.mean) / self.std
225	        return _batch_img
226	
227	    def collate_data(self, data: dict) -> dict:
228	        """Copy data to the target device and perform normalization, padding
229	        and bgr2rgb conversion and stack based on ``BaseDataPreprocessor``.
230	
231	        Collates the data sampled from dataloader into a list of dict and list
232	        of labels, and then copies tensor to the target device.
233	
234	        Args:
235	            data (dict): Data sampled from dataloader.
236	
237	        Returns:
238	            dict: Data in the same format as the model input.
239	        """
240	        data = self.cast_data(data)  # type: ignore
241	
242	        if 'img' in data['inputs']:
243	            _batch_imgs = data['inputs']['img']
244	            # Process data with `pseudo_collate`.
245	            if is_seq_of(_batch_imgs, torch.Tensor):
246	                batch_imgs = []
247	                img_dim = _batch_imgs[0].dim()
248	                for _batch_img in _batch_imgs:
249	                    if img_dim == 3:  # standard img
250	                        _batch_img = self.preprocess_img(_batch_img)
251	                    elif img_dim == 4:
252	                        _batch_img = [
253	                            self.preprocess_img(_img) for _img in _batch_img
254	                        ]
255	
256	                        _batch_img = torch.stack(_batch_img, dim=0)
257	
258	                    batch_imgs.append(_batch_img)
259	
260	                # Pad and stack Tensor.
261	                if img_dim == 3:
262	                    batch_imgs = stack_batch(batch_imgs, self.pad_size_divisor,
263	                                             self.pad_value)
264	                elif img_dim == 4:
265	                    batch_imgs = multiview_img_stack_batch(
266	                        batch_imgs, self.pad_size_divisor, self.pad_value)
267	
268	            # Process data with `default_collate`.
269	            elif isinstance(_batch_imgs, torch.Tensor):
270	                assert _batch_imgs.dim() == 4, (
271	                    'The input of `ImgDataPreprocessor` should be a NCHW '
272	                    'tensor or a list of tensor, but got a tensor with '
273	                    f'shape: {_batch_imgs.shape}')
274	                if self._channel_conversion:
275	                    _batch_imgs = _batch_imgs[:, [2, 1, 0], ...]
276	                # Convert to float after channel conversion to ensure
277	                # efficiency
278	                _batch_imgs = _batch_imgs.float()
279	                if self._enable_normalize:
280	                    _batch_imgs = (_batch_imgs - self.mean) / self.std
281	                h, w = _batch_imgs.shape[2:]
282	                target_h = math.ceil(
283	                    h / self.pad_size_divisor) * self.pad_size_divisor
284	                target_w = math.ceil(
285	                    w / self.pad_size_divisor) * self.pad_size_divisor
286	                pad_h = target_h - h
287	                pad_w = target_w - w
288	                batch_imgs = F.pad(_batch_imgs, (0, pad_w, 0, pad_h),
289	                                   'constant', self.pad_value)
290	            else:
291	                raise TypeError(
292	                    'Output of `cast_data` should be a list of dict '
293	                    'or a tuple with inputs and data_samples, but got '
294	                    f'{type(data)}: {data}')
295	
296	            data['inputs']['imgs'] = batch_imgs
297	
298	        data.setdefault('data_samples', None)
299	
300	        return data
301	
302	    def _get_pad_shape(self, data: dict) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
303	        """Get the pad_shape of each image based on data and
304	        pad_size_divisor."""
305	        # rewrite `_get_pad_shape` for obtaining image inputs.
306	        _batch_inputs = data['inputs']['img']
307	        # Process data with `pseudo_collate`.
308	        if is_seq_of(_batch_inputs, torch.Tensor):
309	            batch_pad_shape = []
310	            for ori_input in _batch_inputs:
311	                if ori_input.dim() == 4:
312	                    # mean multiview input, select one of the
313	                    # image to calculate the pad shape
314	                    ori_input = ori_input[0]
315	                pad_h = int(
316	                    np.ceil(ori_input.shape[1] /
317	                            self.pad_size_divisor)) * self.pad_size_divisor
318	                pad_w = int(
319	                    np.ceil(ori_input.shape[2] /
320	                            self.pad_size_divisor)) * self.pad_size_divisor
321	                batch_pad_shape.append((pad_h, pad_w))
322	        # Process data with `default_collate`.
323	        elif isinstance(_batch_inputs, torch.Tensor):
324	            assert _batch_inputs.dim() == 4, (
325	                'The input of `ImgDataPreprocessor` should be a NCHW tensor '
326	                'or a list of tensor, but got a tensor with shape: '
327	                f'{_batch_inputs.shape}')
328	            pad_h = int(
329	                np.ceil(_batch_inputs.shape[1] /
330	                        self.pad_size_divisor)) * self.pad_size_divisor
331	            pad_w = int(
332	                np.ceil(_batch_inputs.shape[2] /
333	                        self.pad_size_divisor)) * self.pad_size_divisor
334	            batch_pad_shape = [(pad_h, pad_w)] * _batch_inputs.shape[0]
335	        else:
336	            raise TypeError('Output of `cast_data` should be a list of dict '
337	                            'or a tuple with inputs and data_samples, but got '
338	                            f'{type(data)}: {data}')
339	        return batch_pad_shape
340	
341	    @torch.no_grad()
342	    def voxelize(self, points: List[Tensor],
343	                 data_samples: SampleList) -> Dict[str, Tensor]:
344	        """Apply voxelization to point cloud.
345	
346	        Args:
347	            points (List[Tensor]): Point cloud in one data batch.
348	            data_samples: (list[:obj:`Det3DDataSample`]): The annotation data
349	                of every samples. Add voxel-wise annotation for segmentation.
350	
351	        Returns:
352	            Dict[str, Tensor]: Voxelization information.
353	
354	            - voxels (Tensor): Features of voxels, shape is MxNxC for hard
355	              voxelization, NxC for dynamic voxelization.
356	            - coors (Tensor): Coordinates of voxels, shape is Nx(1+NDim),
357	              where 1 represents the batch index.
358	            - num_points (Tensor, optional): Number of points in each voxel.
359	            - voxel_centers (Tensor, optional): Centers of voxels.
360	        """
361	
362	        voxel_dict = dict()
363	
364	        if self.voxel_type == 'hard':
365	            voxels, coors, num_points, voxel_centers = [], [], [], []
366	            for i, res in enumerate(points):
367	                res_voxels, res_coors, res_num_points = self.voxel_layer(res)
368	                res_voxel_centers = (
369	                    res_coors[:, [2, 1, 0]] + 0.5) * res_voxels.new_tensor(
370	                        self.voxel_layer.voxel_size) + res_voxels.new_tensor(
371	                            self.voxel_layer.point_cloud_range[0:3])
372	                res_coors = F.pad(res_coors, (1, 0), mode='constant', value=i)
373	                voxels.append(res_voxels)
374	                coors.append(res_coors)
375	                num_points.append(res_num_points)
376	                voxel_centers.append(res_voxel_centers)
377	
378	            voxels = torch.cat(voxels, dim=0)
379	            coors = torch.cat(coors, dim=0)
380	            num_points = torch.cat(num_points, dim=0)
381	            voxel_centers = torch.cat(voxel_centers, dim=0)
382	
383	            voxel_dict['num_points'] = num_points
384	            voxel_dict['voxel_centers'] = voxel_centers
385	        elif self.voxel_type == 'dynamic':
386	            coors = []
387	            # dynamic voxelization only provide a coors mapping
388	            for i, res in enumerate(points):
389	                res_coors = self.voxel_layer(res)
390	                res_coors = F.pad(res_coors, (1, 0), mode='constant', value=i)
391	                coors.append(res_coors)
392	            voxels = torch.cat(points, dim=0)
393	            coors = torch.cat(coors, dim=0)
394	        elif self.voxel_type == 'cylindrical':
395	            voxels, coors = [], []
396	            for i, (res, data_sample) in enumerate(zip(points, data_samples)):
397	                rho = torch.sqrt(res[:, 0]**2 + res[:, 1]**2)
398	                phi = torch.atan2(res[:, 1], res[:, 0])
399	                polar_res = torch.stack((rho, phi, res[:, 2]), dim=-1)
400	                min_bound = polar_res.new_tensor(
401	                    self.voxel_layer.point_cloud_range[:3])
402	                max_bound = polar_res.new_tensor(
403	                    self.voxel_layer.point_cloud_range[3:])
404	                try:  # only support PyTorch >= 1.9.0
405	                    polar_res_clamp = torch.clamp(polar_res, min_bound,
406	                                                  max_bound)
407	                except TypeError:
408	                    polar_res_clamp = polar_res.clone()
409	                    for coor_idx in range(3):
410	                        polar_res_clamp[:, coor_idx][
411	                            polar_res[:, coor_idx] >
412	                            max_bound[coor_idx]] = max_bound[coor_idx]
413	                        polar_res_clamp[:, coor_idx][
414	                            polar_res[:, coor_idx] <
415	                            min_bound[coor_idx]] = min_bound[coor_idx]
416	                res_coors = torch.floor(
417	                    (polar_res_clamp - min_bound) / polar_res_clamp.new_tensor(
418	                        self.voxel_layer.voxel_size)).int()
419	                self.get_voxel_seg(res_coors, data_sample)
420	                res_coors = F.pad(res_coors, (1, 0), mode='constant', value=i)
421	                res_voxels = torch.cat((polar_res, res[:, :2], res[:, 3:]),
422	                                       dim=-1)
423	                voxels.append(res_voxels)
424	                coors.append(res_coors)
425	            voxels = torch.cat(voxels, dim=0)
426	            coors = torch.cat(coors, dim=0)
427	        elif self.voxel_type == 'minkunet':
428	            voxels, coors = [], []
429	            voxel_size = points[0].new_tensor(self.voxel_layer.voxel_size)
430	            for i, (res, data_sample) in enumerate(zip(points, data_samples)):
431	                res_coors = torch.round(res[:, :3] / voxel_size).int()
432	                res_coors -= res_coors.min(0)[0]
433	
434	                res_coors_numpy = res_coors.cpu().numpy()
435	                inds, point2voxel_map = self.sparse_quantize(
436	                    res_coors_numpy, return_index=True, return_inverse=True)
437	                point2voxel_map = torch.from_numpy(point2voxel_map).cuda()
438	                if self.training and self.max_voxels is not None:
